blocks.title: Common errors
blocks.md: Use the right ordering for $\ce{N2}$ versus $\ce{O2}$. Use one box for each degenerate orbital. A superscript asterisk means antibonding, while an occupancy superscript gives electron count.

blocks.title: Exam practice
blocks.md: For each MO question, write count → order → fill → bond order and magnetism. For ions identify the orbital affected by charging.

blocks.title: Molecular orbitals and bond order
blocks.focus: Separate bonding and antibonding occupancies before calculating bond order.

blocks.title: Oxygen is paramagnetic
blocks.problem: Find bond order and unpaired electrons in $\ce{O2}$.
blocks.answer: Bond order 2 and two unpaired electrons.

steps.title: Apply Hund
steps.md: The last two electrons enter separate π* orbitals.
steps.why: Degenerate orbitals fill singly before pairing.

steps.title: Count
steps.md: Eight bonding and four antibonding electrons give $(8-4)/2=2$.

steps.title: Remove or add
steps.md: The highest occupied electrons in O₂ lie in π* and the same pair has available slots.

steps.title: Update
steps.md: Cation loses an antibonding electron and gains 0.5 in order; anion gains an antibonding electron and loses 0.5.
steps.why: Antibonding electrons enter the formula with a negative sign.

blocks.title: Earlier order for B₂
blocks.problem: What are the predicted bond order and magnetic behavior of $\ce{B2}$?
blocks.answer: Bond order 1 and paramagnetic with two unpaired electrons.

steps.title: Fill six valence electrons
steps.md: Fill σ₂s and σ*₂s with four electrons, then put two in separate π₂p boxes.
steps.why: The π₂p pair lies below σ₂p in this case.

steps.title: Count
steps.md: Four bonding and two antibonding electrons give $(4-2)/2=1$.
steps.why: The two π electrons are unpaired.
